- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model underreacts; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean-reversion zones; if 3 consecutive days show price < 10% below 30-day moving avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate downward trends when sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8); apply 1–3% upward adjustment to align with true volatility.
- If sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model underestimates downside risk; add 2–4% downward buffer to forecast.
